items.t: MicuRx licenses MRX-23 ADC and grants STOPIN platform options to ClearideBio
items.ms: $1M non-refundable upfront; MRX-23 milestones capped at a nominal $223M; options on up to 6 STOPIN programs at up to $125M each ($750M if all are exercised); plus sublicensing revenue share or sales royalties
items.why: MRX-23 is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) candidate from MicuRx; its target and indication were not disclosed. ClearideBio Therapeutics AG (Switzerland) takes exclusive worldwide rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize it across indications. Separately, ClearideBio receives options on up to six targets or target combinations from MicuRx's STOPIN ADC platform, built around a novel camptothecin payload; platform rights vest only after an option is exercised and an exercise fee is paid, while MicuRx keeps the platform's core intellectual property. Headline milestone caps are theoretical maxima, not a valuation or expected revenue, and everything beyond the non-refundable upfront depends on options and milestones being reached. With $1 million paid up front against up to $973 million in headline milestones, this is an option-heavy bet on an unproven payload platform by a Swiss licensee, not a conventional China out-licensing payday.
items.src: Fineline Cube (2026-10-10), reporting MicuRx's SSE announcement

items.t: Asieris grants Theramex exclusive rights to APL-1702 (CEVIRA) in Europe and other markets
items.ms: $15M upfront + $11M near-term regulatory milestone + commercial milestones and tiered sales royalties; subject to conditions precedent
items.why: APL-1702 (CEVIRA) is a photodynamic drug-device for HPV-related cervical precancerous lesions, including CIN. It combines local drug delivery with controlled light activation in an integrated intravaginal device that a clinician fits in the office and the patient removes at home, and is positioned as a non-surgical, tissue-sparing option for women who would otherwise be considered for surgery. China's NMPA approved CEVIRA in March 2026 as a first-in-class non-invasive therapy for cervical precancerous lesions; in Europe it remains investigational. Theramex, a London-based women's health company operating in more than 50 countries, gets exclusive rights in all European countries plus Australia, New Zealand and Turkey, and Asieris keeps the rest of the world. Even the upfront is conditional on a supply agreement, successful manufacturing-site audits, alignment with the upstream licence and a clarification with the European Commission on how the device's clinical value will be assessed. The deal is a bet that an office-based, non-surgical option can win over European regulators and payers; no EU approval has been announced.
items.src: Asieris press release via PR Newswire (2026-10-07)

items.t: Garden Bio and Guangzhou National Laboratory form a joint venture for 25-hydroxycholesterol broad-spectrum antivirals
items.ms: New joint venture run by Garden Biopharma with at least 51%; the rest held by an entity the laboratory designates; phased capital contributions and transfer of IP; no amounts disclosed
items.why: 25-hydroxycholesterol is a natural oxysterol the partners aim to develop, with prodrugs, as a broad-spectrum antiviral. The program is early-stage: English reports describe a new-drug R&D project entering innovative development, without disclosed clinical data. The joint venture is meant to take the candidates through clinical development, registration, manufacturing and commercialization, with Garden Biopharma holding at least 51% and leading day-to-day operations. Garden Biopharma, best known as a vitamin D3 and cholesterol-series manufacturer, frames the deal as its entry into innovative drugs, while Guangzhou National Laboratory contributes the research collaboration. It is a state-laboratory NewCo with a manufacturer in the controlling seat, and whether an oxysterol becomes an approved antiviral has yet to be tested in people.

items.t: Sino Biopharm completes enrollment in Phase 3 registrational trial of inhaled TQC3721 for COPD
items.ms: PACER-III Phase 3 registrational enrollment complete for nebulised TQC3721 in COPD maintenance. HKEX announcement gives no n or endpoints; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07147946 (CTTQ) lists estimated n=666, TQC3721 6 mg/2 ml BID for 24 weeks, primary endpoint mean change in FEV1 AUC from baseline to week 12
items.why: TQC3721 is an inhaled dual PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor from Sino Biopharm's Chia Tai Tianqing (CTTQ). PDE3 is highly expressed in airway smooth muscle and PDE4 in inflammatory cells, so one molecule aims both to relax airways and damp inflammation; the company notes that LAMA/LABA bronchodilators do little for airway inflammation and that inhaled corticosteroids help less in patients with low blood eosinophils while raising pneumonia risk. The nebulised suspension has completed enrollment in PACER-III, the pivotal registrational Phase 3 for COPD maintenance, after Phase 2 PACER-II was published in Chest in 2026; a dry-powder formulation is advancing into Phase 2. A ClinicalTrials.gov record from CTTQ (NCT07147946) describes a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 of 6 mg/2 ml twice daily for 24 weeks in moderate-to-severe COPD, with an estimated 666 participants and a primary endpoint of mean change in FEV1 AUC from baseline to week 12 — but the HKEX announcement does not name that NCT or give trial size. CTTQ says TQC3721 could become the first domestically developed inhaled PDE3/4 inhibitor approved in China; the Phase 3 readout will test whether enrollment completion turns into a registrational win.
items.src: Sino Biopharmaceutical HKEX English announcement (2026-10-08); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07147946

items.t: CSPC updates Phase 1 data for SYS6002 in advanced cervical cancer; 2.4 mg/kg regimen moves into Phase 3
items.ms: Phase 1, 82 patients; confirmed ORR 35.9% (2.4 mg/kg Q2W) and 28.6% (3.6 mg/kg Q3W); median DoR 8.2 and 10.3 months; median PFS 4.1 and 4.3 months; median OS 15.1 and 11.5 months; 2.4 mg/kg Q2W now in Phase 3 (NCT07230626)
items.why: SYS6002 is a Nectin-4 antibody-drug conjugate that delivers the mitotic inhibitor MMAE. It uses enzyme-catalysed site-specific conjugation and a stable linker intended to concentrate toxin in the tumour while limiting systemic exposure. In a nationwide multicentre Phase 1 in China, 82 patients with previously treated advanced cervical cancer received 2.4 mg/kg, every 2 weeks (39 patients) or 3.6 mg/kg every 3 weeks (43 patients); at the 8 May 2026 cutoff (median follow-up 16.1 months), both regimens showed preliminary activity — confirmed ORR, median DoR, median PFS and median OS are in the side box, with PFS and OS reported in months. Treatment-related adverse events were mostly grade 1–2: ocular events were most common (none grade ≥3; no discontinuations for them); interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis 2.4%; rash 20.7% (grade ≥3, 1.2%); peripheral neuropathy 12.2% (all grade 1–2); no treatment-related deaths. Data were a rapid oral at IGCS 2026. The 2.4 mg/kg Q2W regimen has entered Phase 3 (NCT07230626) after immunotherapy, which ClinicalTrials.gov lists as an estimated 412 patients randomized to SYS6002 versus investigator's-choice chemotherapy with overall survival as the primary endpoint. These are single-arm Phase 1 data; that head-to-head Phase 3 will show whether a response rate near 36% turns into a survival benefit.
items.src: CSPC HKEX English announcement (2026-10-08); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07230626

items.t: Novartis takes global rights to Abogen's in vivo mRNA T-cell engager ABO2203
items.ms: $575M upfront + up to ~$7.2B in milestones (including all option exercises) + sales royalties
items.why: ABO2203 is not an in vivo CAR-T. It uses lipid nanoparticles to deliver mRNA encoding a CD19×CD3 T-cell engager, so that the patient's own cells “manufacture” the bispecific to clear B cells. It is in a Phase 1 study in refractory autoimmune disease; the first data made public cover 3 patients with refractory secondary immune thrombocytopenia. Novartis also receives an exclusive option on next-generation assets from Abogen's mRNA/LNP platform. Notably, a $575 million upfront is high for an early Phase 1 asset, suggesting big pharma is willing to bet early on “biologics generated in vivo”, and that mRNA companies have found a new outlet beyond vaccines in autoimmunity.

items.t: GSK buys Chimagen's trispecific T-cell engager for up to $750M
items.ms: Upfront undisclosed + development and commercial milestones (up to $750M combined)
items.why: GSK acquired global rights from Chimagen to a trispecific T-cell engager for multiple myeloma: one arm binds T cells and the other two bind two undisclosed tumor-associated antigens. It is still preclinical; GSK expects it to enter Phase 1 in 2027. The dual-antigen design targets the antigen loss and relapse commonly seen after single-target T-cell engagers (such as BCMA) and CAR-T. This is the second time GSK has bought an asset from Chimagen; the earlier CMG1A46 is a different molecule. Together with Roche's September in-licensing of Simcere Zaiming's CD79a×CD19×CD3, trispecifics are becoming a new deal hotspot in antibody engineering.

items.t: Ivonescimab monotherapy beats pembrolizumab on overall survival in HARMONi-2
items.ms: Phase 3 OS secondary endpoint met with statistical significance
items.why: HARMONi-2 (AK112-303) is a Phase 3 study conducted in China in first-line PD-L1-positive locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, directly comparing ivonescimab (a PD-1×VEGF bispecific) monotherapy with pembrolizumab monotherapy. The primary endpoint, PFS, had already been met (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.38–0.69); this pre-specified analysis shows a statistically significant improvement in overall survival as well, but the press release did not give the OS hazard ratio. A PFS win with OS unknown had been the key question over whether PD-1×VEGF bispecifics can displace Keytruda. Note that these are single-region data; the US and European markets covered by Summit still need support from global studies.

items.t: Simcere Zaiming licenses CD79a×CD19×CD3 trispecific SIM0660 to Roche
items.ms: $75M upfront + development, regulatory and commercial milestones (up to $1.53B total) + tiered double-digit royalties
items.why: SIM0660 is a trispecific T-cell engager: one arm binds CD3 to recruit T cells, while the other two simultaneously bind the B-cell antigens CD79a and CD19. The design aims for potent B-cell depletion while keeping cytokine release low; dual-antigen coverage is also intended to serve patients previously treated with CD20 or CD19 therapies who may have antigen loss. Roche obtains exclusive global rights. The asset is still preclinical or early stage with no specific indication disclosed; the company describes it as aimed at both B-cell malignancies and autoimmune disease. It is another molecular design, after CD19×CD3, in the “T-cell engagers that deplete B cells to treat autoimmunity” theme.

items.t: Lilly to acquire Merida Biosciences for up to $2.9B, entering Graves' disease
items.ms: Upfront undisclosed, milestones included; expected to close by end of 2026
items.why: Merida's approach is to bind pathogenic autoantibodies directly and tag them for clearance, rather than broadly suppressing the immune system. Lead molecule MER511 targets Graves' disease and entered Phase 1 in late 2025, in combination with antithyroid drugs; Lilly also named thyroid eye disease. Merida was founded only in April 2025 with a $121 million Series A and was acquired a little over a year later. According to BioPharma Dive, this is Lilly's 12th company acquisition of 2026 and its 3rd in immunology (after Ventyx and Orna). If the precise “clear only the pathogenic antibodies” strategy holds up, it could avoid the side effects of FcRn inhibitors, which lower all IgG.

items.t: Haisco immunology asset goes into ARCH-founded NewCo Sentivera
items.ms: Upfront and equity combined $75.89M + milestones up to $1.46B + mid-single-digit to low-double-digit royalties
items.why: ARCH Venture Partners and Population Health Partners co-founded the US company Sentivera, which takes exclusive rights outside Greater China to a Haisco immunology asset; Haisco keeps Greater China rights and holds equity in Sentivera. Neither the target nor the modality has been disclosed — only that it addresses type 2 inflammatory diseases, has just received a Chinese IND, and showed anti-inflammatory activity and good safety preclinically. This is the classic NewCo playbook: the Chinese side trades the asset for cash plus equity, while a top US VC builds the team to run overseas clinical development. Upfront and equity together are less than 5% of the headline total; most of the value depends on later milestones.

items.t: J&J locks up Sail Biomedicines' in vivo CAR-T with an equity stake and an acquisition option
items.m: $2.58B total if the acquisition option is exercised
items.ms: $785M up front in total (incl. $465M equity investment) + up to $140M development milestones + acquisition option
items.why: Sail's platform engineers immune cells directly inside the patient to generate CAR-T, using its eRNA and nanoparticle delivery technology and skipping cell collection, ex vivo engineering and reinfusion. The collaboration first advances Sail's lead immune-mediated disease program (molecule not disclosed), aiming for an “immune reset” rather than long-term symptom control. J&J pays $785 million up front and holds an option to acquire the whole company; if exercised, the deal totals $2.58 billion. After AbbVie bought Capstan and Lilly bought Kelonia, in vivo CAR-T has become a standard big-pharma bet in autoimmunity.

items.t: argenx to acquire Forte for $2.2B, adding anti-CD122 antibody FB102
items.ms: $77 per share cash tender offer, no milestones; expected to close in Q3 2026
items.why: FB102 is a first-in-class anti-CD122 (IL-2/IL-15 receptor β chain) monoclonal antibody designed to suppress the activity of pathogenic T cells and NK cells. Phase 1b vitiligo data released on July 9 showed a statistically significant benefit; a Phase 1b in celiac disease was reported positive in 2025, Phase 2 data are expected in the second half of 2026, and alopecia areata is also a planned direction. The price represents a premium of about 86% to the volume-weighted average price after the vitiligo data. argenx built its business on the FcRn inhibitor Vyvgart; this deal extends its immunology footprint from B-cell/antibody-mediated diseases to T-cell-driven skin and gut diseases.

items.t: GemPharmatech and Humlab partner on global distribution of humanized mouse models
items.ms: Global distribution agreement; financial terms, duration and exclusivity not disclosed
items.why: GemPharmatech is a leading Chinese genetically engineered mouse company and says it holds more than 30,000 knockout, conditional knockout, humanized and immunodeficient strains; Humlab is a Singapore-based developer of humanized mice. The agreement covers both companies' existing and newly developed humanized strains, including aging models, autoimmune and inflammatory models such as IBD and systemic lupus erythematosus, MASH metabolic models, oncology and infection models, and a new humanized-liver mouse. With the FDA pushing to reduce animal testing, growth for animal-model companies is shifting toward more “human-like” humanized models. Humlab's statements about engraftment efficiency are the company's own; the release did not include data.

items.t: Avere in-licenses Hansoh's oral IL-23 drug, lists via NextCure reverse merger and raises $320M
items.m: License up to $2.3B; concurrent $320M private placement
items.ms: License: $120M upfront + up to $2.18B milestones + royalties; private placement led by Fairmount and Hansoh
items.why: Avere takes rights outside Greater China to Hansoh's oral IL-23 inhibitor AVR-001 and, at the same time, reverse-merges with NextCure to list on Nasdaq (ticker AVRX); NextCure's existing shareholders own just over 1% of the combined company. AVR-001 is positioned as an oral psoriasis drug with a longer dosing interval than J&J's daily oral IL-23 drug; Hansoh has started a Phase 2b in China and Avere has applied to begin US clinical trials. The team comes from Akero, which Novo Nordisk acquired for $4.7 billion. License, reverse merger and financing completed in one move — with Hansoh as both licensor and lead investor — is a new variant of the NewCo model.

items.t: AstraZeneca and CSPC partner on kidney-disease siRNA
items.why: The two companies will jointly discover and develop small-interfering-RNA drugs against two undisclosed kidney-disease targets, using CSPC's siRNA discovery platform and delivery tools that can carry drugs to organs beyond the liver, plus CSPC's AI molecular-design models and automated high-throughput screening. AstraZeneca may choose global or ex-China exclusive rights; CSPC retains China rights to one of the assets. siRNA has so far been largely limited to liver targets (GalNAc conjugation), and kidney delivery is widely seen as the industry's next hurdle. With only $30 million up front, this is an early discovery deal whose value rests mainly on later stages.
items.src: Fierce Biotech (2026-07-03, citing CSPC's July 2 announcement)

items.t: Insilico Medicine and Takeda sign AI drug discovery collaboration
items.ms: Project initiation fee, near-term payments and milestones of ~$60M + later success milestones (~$600M total) + tiered royalties
items.why: Insilico will use its Pharma.AI platform to discover molecules for Takeda that meet pre-agreed scientific and early-development criteria; Takeda is responsible for clinical validation and receives exclusive global development, manufacturing and commercialization rights to the selected molecules. The release does not limit therapeutic areas, saying only that it covers Takeda's therapeutic areas (Takeda's core areas include gastroenterology and inflammation, rare diseases, oncology, neuroscience and vaccines). Insilico is one of the few companies with an AI-discovered molecule in Phase 2; this deal shows big pharma–AI partnerships moving from “platform validation” to routine pay-per-program business.

items.t: Lilly to acquire in vivo CAR-T company Kelonia for up to $7B
items.ms: $3.25B upfront + ~$3.75B in clinical, regulatory and commercial milestones; expected to close in H2 2026
items.why: Kelonia's iGPS platform uses engineered lentivirus-like particles to enter T cells in vivo, so the patient's body generates its own CAR-T. Lead program KLN-1010 is a single-IV-infusion gene therapy that generates anti-BCMA CAR-T for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; early Phase 1 data were presented in the plenary session of the 2025 ASH Annual Meeting. Lilly plans to extend the platform to other hematologic cancers, solid tumors and other serious diseases. The $3.25 billion upfront is a record in in vivo CAR-T and exceeds the total price of AbbVie's acquisition of Capstan, showing the approach has moved from proof of concept to big pharma competing for assets.
